exercises.name: PLYOSOFT box-supported one-arm row
exercises.main: Latissimus dorsi: draws the upper arm back toward the trunk.
exercises.secondary: Rhomboids and middle trapezius control the shoulder blade; rear deltoid and elbow flexors assist the pull.
exercises.base: Abdominals and spinal stabilizers resist rotation. Hips, thighs and ankle muscles steady both feet; the other arm supports the torso.
exercises.setup: Use a stable PLYOSOFT box and a secure front rack anchor near the working hand's starting height. Clip one handle to one continuous pull line; keep the recoil path clear.
exercises.position: Plant both feet in a comfortable stagger. Support the opposite palm under its shoulder. Incline from the hips; keep neck and trunk aligned, knees soft.
exercises.move: Gently brace while breathing. Exhale and guide the working elbow toward the lower ribs; keep the shoulder away from the ear.
exercises.range: Stop before the torso twists, the shoulder rolls forward or the elbow has to travel far behind the body. Return slowly to a softly extended arm.
exercises.check: Both feet and the support hand stay planted. Shorten the pull or reduce resistance if you shrug, jerk or rotate.
exercises.easier: Rehearse unloaded, use less tension, or use a more upright supported row if the hinge is uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Supported single-arm chest press
exercises.origin: Supported adaptation to complement the personal pull/triceps library
exercises.main: Pectoralis major: moves the upper arm forward and across the chest.
exercises.secondary: Triceps extend the elbow; anterior deltoid assists. Scapular muscles guide the shoulder blade.
exercises.base: Trunk muscles resist rotation; the box and planted feet stabilize the pelvis and legs.
exercises.setup: Use a stable non-rolling PLYOSOFT box and a secure anchor behind you near chest height. Keep the band beside the arm, away from the neck and face.
exercises.position: Sit tall with both feet planted. Start with the handle beside the chest, neutral wrist and elbow below shoulder height. Let the shoulder blade move naturally.
exercises.move: Breathe out and press forward smoothly while keeping ribs and pelvis steady. Do not lean or twist to finish.
exercises.range: Finish before the elbow locks; return only as far as the shoulder remains comfortable. Avoid a deep forced stretch behind the torso.
exercises.check: If the ribs flare, shoulder pinches or trunk turns, shorten the range and lower the load.
exercises.easier: Use an unloaded press rehearsal or a comfortable wall press-up instead.

exercises.name: Seated straight-bar pressdown
exercises.main: Triceps brachii: straightens the elbow.
exercises.secondary: Forearm muscles steady the grip and wrist; shoulder muscles hold the upper arms beside the torso.
exercises.base: Trunk muscles hold a quiet seated posture; both feet and the box provide support.
exercises.setup: Use one secure high rack anchor, one rated pull line and a straight-bar attachment. Position a stable PLYOSOFT box so the line stays in front of the body.
exercises.position: Plant both feet; sit tall. Keep upper arms beside the ribs and wrists in line with forearms. Choose a grip you can hold without strain.
exercises.move: Exhale and extend the elbows without pushing the shoulders down with body weight. Keep the upper arms nearly still.
exercises.range: Stop short of snapping the elbows straight. Return gradually into comfortable elbow flexion without letting the bar rise toward the face.
exercises.check: Avoid a rocking torso, bent wrists or moving the whole upper arm. Reduce load if the elbows or grip lose control.
exercises.easier: Rehearse the elbow motion unloaded or use a lighter single-handle variation matched to current tolerance.

exercises.main: Middle deltoid contributes to lifting the arm out to the side.
exercises.secondary: Supraspinatus assists the lift; rotator-cuff and scapular muscles coordinate the shoulder.
exercises.base: Trunk muscles and planted feet keep the torso quiet; a box supports the seated base.
exercises.setup: Begin without a band. Use a stable PLYOSOFT box with room at both sides. This is a comfortable movement rehearsal, not a heavy raise.
exercises.position: Sit tall, feet planted, elbows softly bent and hands relaxed. Start with arms beside the body.
exercises.move: Lift in a slightly forward plane with thumbs comfortably forward or up. Breathe normally and keep the neck relaxed.
exercises.range: Use a small pain-free arc below shoulder height; stop sooner if the shoulder hikes, pinches or the torso leans.
exercises.check: Do not force the arms overhead or use a shrug to gain height. A smaller controlled arc is the aim.
exercises.easier: Move one arm at a time through a shorter comfortable arc, or omit if symptoms occur.

exercises.name: Seated brace with normal breathing
exercises.main: Abdominal wall: develops gentle trunk stiffness while breathing.
exercises.secondary: Deep spinal stabilizers cooperate with the abdominal wall; breathing muscles continue their normal work.
exercises.base: box contact and planted feet steady the pelvis. Hip and leg muscles provide light postural support.
exercises.setup: Use a stable PLYOSOFT box. No band is required; this is a low-effort control drill.
exercises.position: Sit comfortably tall with ribs over pelvis and both feet on the floor. Keep shoulders relaxed and avoid arching the back.
exercises.move: Gently firm the midsection as if preparing for a light nudge. Take slow normal breaths without bearing down.
exercises.range: Hold only while breathing and posture stay easy. Release fully between attempts; no trunk movement is needed.
exercises.check: Do not suck the stomach in forcefully, brace maximally or hold the breath.
exercises.easier: Use a lighter contraction for fewer breaths with back support if comfortable.

exercises.name: Supported sit-to-stand
exercises.main: Quadriceps and gluteus maximus raise the body from the box.
exercises.secondary: Hamstrings and hip muscles coordinate the hip and knee movement.
exercises.base: Trunk and ankle muscles help balance the body over the feet; the box marks the return position.
exercises.setup: Place a stable PLYOSOFT box on a non-slip floor. Choose a height that lets both feet rest flat.
exercises.position: Sit near the front edge. Place feet under the knees and hands on the thighs.
exercises.move: Lean forward from the hips enough to bring weight over the feet, then stand smoothly. Breathe out during the effort.
exercises.range: Finish upright with soft knees. Bend hips and knees to return under control; touch down rather than falling into the PLYOSOFT box.
exercises.check: Avoid knees collapsing inward, breath-holding or pushing through pain. Use a higher seat or hand assistance.
exercises.easier: Use a higher PLYOSOFT box or more hand support; keep the same controlled return.

exercises.name: Seated single-leg band curl
exercises.main: Hamstrings bend the knee, drawing the heel back.
exercises.secondary: Gastrocnemius can assist knee flexion. Ankle-positioning muscles hold the foot position; hip muscles keep the thigh aligned.
exercises.base: box, opposite planted foot and trunk muscles steady the pelvis. The working thigh stays supported.
exercises.setup: Sit at the front edge of a stable PLYOSOFT box. Attach the ankle cuff to the low front line.
exercises.position: Sit tall with the working thigh supported. Start with that heel forward and the knee softly extended; keep the ankle comfortable.
exercises.move: Exhale and slide or draw the heel back by bending the knee. Keep the thigh and pelvis quiet rather than pulling with the hip.
exercises.range: Keep the heel path in front of the box. Extend the knee slowly without sudden recoil.
exercises.check: If the PLYOSOFT box shifts, cuff slips, knee hurts or pelvis rocks, stop and reset; use less tension.
exercises.easier: Rehearse the heel slide without a band. Do not add resistance until the cuff and anchor are appropriate.

kuzaro.rule: One of each rating per kit; use one limb at a time where matching pairs are unavailable. Level limits are ceilings, not target loads.

hpygn.rule: Separate Pilates kit. Each level uses matched left/right bundles. Previous 2 x 65 per side is a historical configuration, not the definition of R1, R2 or R3.

loadRule: Select resistance only after confirming comfortable motion, control, anchor/attachment ratings and current tolerance. Bodyweight or unloaded practice is valid. A 35 lb labelled band may already be too much. Label sums are not measured hand force or hardware ratings.
